name: Tiger Woods
hook: Golf's biggest name — the green jacket, the Stanford years, and the comeback from a car crash.

facts.label: Eldrick "Tiger" Woods
facts.statement: His given name is Eldrick; the nickname Tiger honors his father's Vietnam War buddy, and he calls himself "Cablinasian."

facts.label: Stanford
facts.statement: He competed for Stanford — "the Farm" — as did John McEnroe and Janet Evans, before leaving for the pro tour.

facts.label: the 1997 Masters
facts.statement: He became the youngest ever to win the Masters in 1997 at Augusta, taking the green jacket at 21 and winning again in 2001 and 2002.

facts.label: U.S. Amateur
facts.statement: He won the U.S. Amateur three straight times, taking the 1996 title at Pumpkin Ridge before turning pro; in 1994 he had been its youngest winner.

facts.label: Vijay Singh
facts.statement: Fijian-born Vijay Singh beat him by six strokes at the 2000 Masters and displaced him as world No. 1 in 2003.

facts.label: the 2022 Masters
facts.statement: A year after a serious car crash, he returned to competition at the 2022 Masters in Augusta.

facts.label: Wheaties
facts.statement: A 22-page booklet, "The Making of a Champion," came free on a million boxes of Wheaties.
